entry.question:
## Physical scenario

A light detector has an absorbing area of \( 2.00\times10^{-6}\,\text{m}^2 \) and absorbs 50\% of the incident light, which is at wavelength \( 600\,\text{nm} \). The detector faces an isotropic source, \( 12.0\,\text{m} \) from the source. The energy \( E \) emitted by the source versus time \( t \) is given in figure \( (E_s = 7.2\,\text{nJ},\,t_s = 2.0\,\text{s}) \).

## Question

At what rate are photons absorbed by the detector?

## Answer choices

- A: A: 12.0photons/s

- B: B: 3.0photons/s

- C: C: 6.0photons/s

- D: D: 9.0photons/s

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image is a graph with the x-axis labeled as \( t \) (s) and the y-axis labeled as \( E \) (nJ). There is a diagonal line in pink that starts from the origin (0, 0) and rises linearly up to the point \( (t_s, E_s) \). At this point, two dashed lines extend horizontally and vertically: one from \( E_s \) to the y-axis and another from \( t_s \) to the x-axis. This indicates a relationship where energy \( E \) increases linearly over time \( t \) until it reaches the specified energy level \( E_s \) at time \( t_s \).
